title: Cross-locale Regression Kit: CJK & RTL + Formatting Checks
content:
Purpose:
This is a working regression/eval kit intended for model onboarding runs that focus on: CJK tokenization and cultural formatting, RTL bidi correctness (Arabic/Hebrew), translation fidelity across low-resource pairs, and locale-specific numeric/date/currency formatting. The goal is to provide a compact, runnable prompt bank and checklist that engineers and evaluators can use during onboarding and nightly regression sweeps.

Scope & audience:
- Primary: applied-ml engineers and model reviewers onboarding new model weights to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Secondary: product engineers running integration checks that depend on locale-sensitive formatting.
- Not included: large-scale human evaluation results (these are linked by reference).

Quick run instructions (developer flow):
1) Fetch prompt batch: scripts/eval_runner --batch cross-locale-quick --model <candidate> --out results/<model>/cross-locale.csv
2) Automated metrics: run scripts/compute_locale_scores.py --in results/<model>/cross-locale.csv --out metrics/<model>/cross-locale.json
3) Manual review: sample 200 examples (see sampling tags below) and upload to eval UI (link in linked_artifacts).
Notes: test harness expects UTF-8 output. For Private deployments, ensure KMS service account has evaluator role.

Evaluation rubric (automated + manual):
- Translation quality: BLEU >= 18 for en->zh/ja and en->ar (thresholds are relaxed for some low-resource pairs). For short string tests use chrF and exact-match for numeric/currency segments.
- Bidi correctness: heuristics for visual order preservation + manual spot checks; expect no raw LTR punctuation interleaved inside Arabic/Hebrew runs.
- Formatting exactness: dates/numbers/currency should exactly match target locale formats (see test cases). Failures are considered critical when downstream parsers break (e.g., JSON with wrong decimal separators).
- Regression gating: any drop > 5% relative to baseline on translation BLEU or any new critical formatting failure blocks rollout.

Prompt batches included in this kit (short descriptions and example prompts):
1) CJK-short-contexts (50 prompts) 
   - Focus: tokenization edge cases, mixed full-width/half-width punctuation, mixed numeral sets.
   - Example: "Translate to Chinese (Simplified) and preserve numeric tokens: 'Payment due: $1,234.56 on 2026-03-15.'"
   - Expected output snippet: "付款到期日：2026年3月15日，应付金额：$1,234.56。" (numbers may be localized depending on test variant)

2) Japanese-era-and-iso (20 prompts)
   - Focus: Gregorian vs. Japanese era date formatting, honorific name ordering.
   - Example: "Format date '2025-05-01' in Japanese short form with era and in ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and return both, separated by ' | '."
   - Expected: "令和7年5月1日 | 2025-05-01"

3) Chinese-numerals-variants (30 prompts)
   - Focus: output in Arabic numerals, full-width numerals, and traditional Chinese numerals as options.
   - Example: "Represent '3050' in three formats: Arabic, full-width, and Chinese traditional numerals."

4) RTL-bidi-sanity (60 prompts)
   - Focus: Arabic and Hebrew sentences containing embedded LTR segments (URLs, email, code), punctuation, and parentheses.
   - Example: "Translate the sentence into Arabic and keep the URL intact: 'See docs at https://docs.example.com/path (version 2.0). Please update.'"
   - Expected behavior: URL remains LTR sequence, surrounding Arabic words render with correct bidi markers; parentheses orientation should follow visual rendering rules.

5) Translation-fidelity-low-resource (40 prompts)
   - Focus: en<->ar, en<->he, en<->zh, en<->ja, including idiomatic phrases and named-entity preservation.
   - Example: "Translate to Arabic: 'The conference keynote emphasized time-to-market over feature parity.'"

6) Locale-formatting-exact (50 prompts)
   - Focus: decimals/comma separators, thousands separators, currency symbols placement, percent signs, ordinal indicators, day/month name localization.
   - Example: "Format the following amount 12345.67 for French (fr-FR), German (de-DE), Arabic (ar-EG), and Japanese (ja-JP)."
   - Expected: fr-FR: "12 345,67 €" or variant depending on symmetric rules; de-DE: "12.345,67 €"; ar-EG: localized digits or Arabic-Indic digits depending on variant.

7) Parser-compatibility-samples (15 prompts)
   - Focus: outputs intended to be machine-parsed later (JSON snippets, date tokens, locale-aware CSV).
   - Example: "Return a JSON object with keys: date_iso, amount, currency for the following: 'March 3rd, 2026 - $2,500.00'"
   - Expected: exact JSON token order and quoting; failures flagged as critical.

Scoring details and thresholds (recommended):
- Translation BLEU/chrf: per-language baselines recorded in metrics/baselines.csv. Gate if candidate < baseline - 5%.
- Formatting exact-match: 100% for critical parser outputs, 90% acceptable for display-only strings.
- Bidi heuristics: automated checks for stray LTR punctuation inside RTL runs, percentage of clean renders > 98%.
- Human spot-check: sample 50 instances per major language group; allow up to 3% human-reported regressions before escalation.

Regression history tracking (how to annotate failures):
- Record every failure with tags: failing-category (translation/formatting/bidi/parse), test-id (from this kit), model-version, commit-hash, and short note.
- Use JIRA-ML-4821 for gating-critical regressions.

Data provenance and licensing:
- Synthetic prompts authored by applied-ml team (author names in collaborators).
- Example parallel references derived from OpenSubtitles (CC-BY), Tatoeba (CC-BY), and a small internal human-translated seed set (licensed to Redwood). Do not export seed set outside company.

Known limitations (quick callouts):
- BLEU is brittle for very short strings; prefer chrF for short segments.
- Some Japanese era conversions ambiguous for historical dates — tests focus on modern dates only.
- Locale formatting variations across countries (e.g., non-breaking spaces in French thousands) will create false positives; see notes below on normalization rules.

Normalization rules for scoring (important):
- Strip Unicode bidi control characters before token-level BLEU calculations but keep them for visual/manual checks.
- Normalize all non-breaking spaces to a single NBSP codepoint for French tests.
- Treat full-width/half-width punctuation as distinct when the test variant requires it; otherwise convert to half-width for lenient checks.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Decide canonical behavior for Arabic-Indic digits vs. Western digits in ar-EG tests (product preference conflict). (Owner: Rashid)
- Add more Southeast Asian scripts (Thai/Myanmar) in next iteration.
- Create small human-eval rubric for politeness/tone in Japanese translations.

Quick notes for reviewers:
- When a formatting failure triggers, reproduce on both Hosted API and Dedicated staging to rule out client-side transforms.
- Record exact model prompt (including system instructions) and response context window.

Appendix: sampling tags for manual review upload:
- sample:high-risk-formatting (dates, JSON outputs)
- sample:rtl-bidi-with-url
- sample:cjk-mixed-punc
- sample:low-resource-idiom

Contact and follow-up:
- Slack: #applied-ml-evals
- Owners: Sofia Nguyen (sofia@redwood.example), Kenji Watanabe

End of kit.
